title: DFT-LDA total-energy calculations for Al(111) slab with adatom
action: Set up a five-layer Al(111) slab with at least 8 Å vacuum and a surface supercell large enough to isolate the adatom (e.g., 3×3 or 4×4). Using an open-source plane-wave DFT code with LDA and an Al pseudopotential, perform self-consistent total-energy calculations, allowing relaxation, for the clean slab and for the slab with a single Al adatom placed at the hcp, fcc, bridge, and top sites. Also compute the total energy of an isolated Al atom in a large cell with the same cutoff. Record key total energies and relaxed geometries in a log file for reproducibility audit.
description: This step runs the DFT calculations whose output total energies are needed to derive adsorption energies and diffusion barrier.

title: Compute site-resolved adsorption energies
action: From the total energies obtained in step 0, compute the adsorption energy for each site as E_site = E_total(slab+adatom) - E_total(clean slab) - E_isolated_atom. Also extract the adatom height above the top substrate layer for each site. Report the results for hcp, fcc, bridge, and top sites.
description: CSV file with columns: site (hcp, fcc, bridge, top), adsorption_energy_eV (float), height_A (float). One row per site. Energy is relative to the free atom; heights are in Å.

title: Compute self-diffusion barrier
action: Using the adsorption energies from step 1, determine the self-diffusion barrier for an isolated Al adatom on flat Al(111). The barrier is the energy difference between the stable adsorption minimum (hcp) and the saddle point along the hcp–bridge–fcc path. Take the saddle energy as the higher of the bridge and fcc energies. Report the barrier value in eV.
description: A single-line text file containing the diffusion barrier in eV as a floating-point number.
output_schema: One line: floating-point number (barrier in eV).
